module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Central trinomial coefficients

Central trinomial coefficients: largest coefficient of $(1 + x + x^2)^n$, which is the coefficient
of $x^n$ in the expansion of $(1 + x + x^2)^n$.

*References:*
- [A002426](https://oeis.org/A002426)-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA2426

/-- Central trinomial coefficients:
$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \binom{n}{2k} \binom{2k}{k}$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n / 2 + 1), n.choose (2 * k) * (2 * k).choose k

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 7 := by rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 19 := by rfl

/--
An integer $n > 3$ is prime if and only if $a(n) \equiv 1 \pmod{n^2}$.
We have verified this for $n$ up to $8 \cdot 10^5$, and proved that $a(p) \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$
for any prime $p > 3$ (cf. A277640).
- Zhi-Wei Sun, Nov 30 2016-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 < n) :
    n.Prime ↔ a n ≡ 1 [MOD n ^ 2] := by
  sorry

end OeisA2426

sources_consulted: OEIS A002426, including Sun’s November 30, 2016 conjecture and the sequence formulas, read through the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A002/A002426.seq
OEIS A277640, read through the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A277/A277640.seq

Hao Pan and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Supercongruences for central trinomial coefficients,” Frontiers in Combinatorics and Number Theory 2 (2026), 55–62, especially equation (1.1) and Remark 1.1. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2012.05121
review.notes:
Checked all seven declarations. The definition of a matches the central trinomial coefficient formula, including the inclusive upper bound floor(n/2) and the value at n = 0. All five initial-value theorems match OEIS. OeisA2426.conjecture states precisely Sun’s criterion, with the correct domain n > 3, biconditional, and modulus n².

Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled successfully. They verified all 201 coefficients for 0 ≤ n ≤ 200 against the official b-file, checked the criterion for 4 ≤ n ≤ 200, and confirmed the excluded boundary cases n = 0, 1, 2, 3 fail the unrestricted criterion. The summation bounds and ordinary remainder interpretation were also verified in Lean.

The research-open status agrees with the sources: the 2026 Pan–Sun paper still presents this primality characterization as a conjecture in Remark 1.1. Its proved supercongruences do not establish the converse. Direct OEIS entry pages were browser-challenge blocked; their records were read through OEIS’s public data mirror, and the b-file was accessible directly.
